problem: VLN agents learn to ground words such as 'butterfly sculpture' or 'banister rail' only from about 14k R2R path-instruction pairs. That data is small and only mentions objects found in the training environments. Path ranking in the pre-explored (beam-search) setting has relied on generative follower or speaker models trained from scratch, with ImageNet as the only external data.
motivation: Collecting embodied path-instruction data is expensive, while web image-text corpora such as Conceptual Captions (3.3M pairs) are free and abundant. It was unclear whether grounding learned from curated, aesthetically framed web photos would transfer to embodied panoramic views, where framing depends on the agent's position. The paper tests this directly with a model that has the same architecture as ViLBERT, so the pretrained weights can be reused.
key_idea: Treat VLN in pre-explored environments as a discriminative path-instruction compatibility scoring problem. The scorer, VLN-BERT, extends ViLBERT and is trained with a curriculum: BERT language pretraining, then ViLBERT pretraining on Conceptual Captions, then masked multimodal pretraining on R2R, then fine-tuning to pick the correct path among beam-search candidates.
insight:
The curriculum ablation (Table 1, val-unseen SR) gives these results:
- No pretraining: 30.52.
- BERT initialization: 45.17, the largest single gain; language understanding matters a lot.
- Adding web visual grounding alone: 49.64 (+4.5).
- Adding R2R action-grounding MLM alone: 50.02 (+4.9).
- Both stages in series: 59.26 (+14.1), a superadditive effect.

Removing only the Conceptual Captions stage costs 9.2 SR, so disembodied web grounding transfers and also makes the embodied pretraining stage more effective. The discriminative scorer is complementary to the generative speaker and follower. Adding it to a speaker+follower ensemble gives +5.7 SR, versus +1.2 for an extra follower and +2.7 for an extra speaker. Qualitatively, gradient saliency shows the model grounds rare or unseen words (e.g. 'antelope head', 'freezers'), and the model without the web stage misses them ('mini fridge', 'massage table').
method: Path-selection formulation: in a pre-explored environment, beam search with the EnvDrop follower generates up to 30 candidate paths per instruction (over 99% of candidate sets contain a successful path). VLN-BERT scores each (path, instruction) pair and the argmax is chosen.

VLN-BERT architecture: a ViLBERT two-stream transformer (12-layer BERT-BASE vision and language streams, 6 co-attention layers). The input is + regions for each panorama in the trajectory, followed by + instruction tokens + . The score is s = W(h_CLS ⊙ h_IMG).

Panoramic region features: each panorama is rendered as 36 perspective views (600x600, 80° FOV). Bottom-up attention Faster R-CNN (Visual Genome) extracts regions. Regions centred more than 20° off the view centre are dropped, and similar regions are deduplicated by feature cosine distance plus heading/elevation difference, keeping at most 100 regions per panorama.

Trajectory positional encoding: an 11-d spatial vector per region (normalized box corners, area, elevation, heading relative to the agent's current and next direction, encoded as cos/sin) is projected to 2048-d with W^S. A learned panorama-index embedding W^P is added, and both are summed with the visual feature.

Training objective with mined negatives: a 4-way multiple-choice task (1 successful path plus 3 unsuccessful ones, sampled from 30 follower beams, success = within 3 m) trained with softmax cross-entropy. Beam-search negatives give semantically meaningful hard negatives.

Three-stage internet-to-embodied curriculum: (1) language stream initialized from BERT (Wikipedia + BooksCorpus); (2) full model initialized from ViLBERT trained on Conceptual Captions with masked multimodal modelling and alignment; (3) masked multimodal modelling on R2R path-instruction pairs for 50 epochs; then 20 epochs of path-selection fine-tuning (Adam, learning rate 4e-5, batch 64).
Ensembling: for the leaderboard, VLN-BERT scores are linearly combined with EnvDrop speaker and follower scores, with weights α and β chosen by grid search on val-unseen.

numbers_note: SPL is printed as a fraction (e.g. 0.55) and converted to 0-100 here. Val-split numbers are path-selection metrics on the chosen path only; test numbers include the beam-search exploration path. Early stopping and the ensemble weights were tuned on val-unseen.
results: In single-model path re-ranking on R2R val-unseen, VLN-BERT reaches 59.26 SR / 0.55 SPL. That is 4.6 SR above the strongest single baseline, the EnvDrop speaker (54.66); the EnvDrop follower gets 52.36. Adding VLN-BERT to the speaker+follower ensemble gives 73.61 SR on val-unseen, 3.0 points above the best alternative three-model ensemble (70.58), and 73% SR on the R2R test-unseen leaderboard, beating EnvDrop (69%) and concurrent AuxRN (71%) among beam-search methods. In the ablation, the web image-text stage adds 9.2 SR on top of language + action pretraining.
limitations: Works only as a re-ranker in the pre-explored / beam-search setting. It is not an online navigation agent, and the leaderboard entry has a huge path length (687 m) and SPL of 0.01 because the exploration path is included.

Depends on the EnvDrop follower to generate candidates (performance is bounded by candidate coverage) and requires scoring each full trajectory with a large transformer; Stage 3 training takes about 66 h on 8 Titan X GPUs.
Early stopping and ensemble weights are tuned on val-unseen, and the evidence for grounding transfer is only qualitative (gradient saliency).
